info.bio:
The Cranberries es una banda irlandesa de rock, formada en Limerick en 1989 bajo el nombre de The Cranberry Saw Us, más tarde cambiado por la vocalista Dolores O'Riordan. Aunque muchas veces es asociada con rock alternativo, el sonido de la banda también incorpora elementos de indie, indie pop, Rock, post-punk y pop rock.

The Cranberries saltó a la fama internacional en la década de 1990 con su álbum debut,Everybody Else Is Doing It, So Why Can't We?

scenes.name: Psicodelia británica de los noventa
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La edad de oro de la psicodelia británica no fueron los sesenta sino los noventa: las raves crean una demanda inagotable de música inducida por (o para) las drogas. La versión pop (Telescopes, Inspiral Carpets, Verve, Sundial, Auteurs, Kula Shaker), las más sofisticadas (Curve, Cranberries, Rollerskate Skinny, Beta Band, dEUS, Gorky's Zygotic Mynci), el space-rock libre (Porcupine Tree, Terminal Cheesecake, Heads), los últimos shoegazers (Ride, Swervedriver, Spectrum y E.A.R. de Sonic Boom, Spiritualized de Jason Pierce, Flying Saucer Attack, encuentro de shoegazing y ambient) y el dream-pop (Lush, Pale Saints, Slowdive, Catherine Wheel, Bark Psychosis).

podcast.title: Breakup Date (September 15, 2003)
podcast.body: While an exact date is difficult to pinpoint, September 15, 2003, is considered approximately correct for when the members scattered to pursue solo endeavors, being "sick of each other" and "tired of being in the band." "It's hard to find an exact date, but September 15th 2003 seems to be about right. All the members scattered after that date to do their own thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Son's Confirmation Catalyst (June 2009)
podcast.body: Dolores O'Riordan invited Mike and Fergal, along with their families, to her son's confirmation in June. This was her first time seeing Fergal since their separation. The presence of all their children, who didn't remember The Cranberries, also contributed to the reunion desire. "And so then my son then made his confirmation in June and I invited Mike Ferg and no with their wives and children."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Trinity College Philosophical Society Event (2009)
podcast.body: The reunion process began when Trinity College made Dolores O'Riordan a member of their philosophical society and invited her to perform. She asked Mike and Noel Hogan and Fergal Lawler to play with her, marking their first reunion. "Trinity College made me a member of their philosophical society and they wanted me to do a couple of songs, you know?"

podcast.title: Dolores O'Riordan's Death (2018)
podcast.body: Dolores O'Riordan was found dead in her London hotel room around 9 AM on January 15, 2018. Investigations revealed she had been drinking heavily the previous night, with several mini-bar bottles and an empty champagne bottle found in her room. She apparently drew a bath while in her pajamas, laid down, passed out, and died below the surface of the water, with no evidence of drug abuse found. "But as we all know, at around 9 that morning, Dolores was found dead in her London hotel room."

podcast.title: Cancelled Tours and Unexplained Concert Stops
podcast.body: The band had several tours cancelled and concerts halted without clear explanations, leading to various incorrect speculations and legends about Dolores O'Riordan's health. "había habido varias giras de los gran barris que habían sido canceladas y conciertos que habían sido parados además como sin explicaciones."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Cultural Impact on 90s Generation
podcast.body: The first three Cranberries albums were widely owned by "90s kids," often placed alongside records by popular bands like Pearl Jam and Oasis, signifying their significant cultural footprint. "Everyone had those first three cranberries albums right next to their records by Pearl Jam and Oasis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dissolution due to Personal Problems
podcast.body: The band experienced a decline in the new century, culminating in their dissolution around 2001 due to significant personal problems among the members. "el nuevo siglo ya vino un poco como la cuesta abajo ... había bastantes problemas personales entre ellos que los llevaban a disolverse."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Distinctive Style and Lyrical Depth
podcast.body: The band maintained a very personal style, never compromising their artistic integrity for chart success. Dolores O'Riordan's lyrics were consistently intense, intimate, and never as banal as those found in many contemporary bands. "no fue una banda que se echó a las listas a cualquier precio con lo cual seguió como manteniendo un estilo muy personal las letras de dolores siguieron siendo como muy bastante intensas y bastante intimistas."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Dolores O'Riordan's Global Fame and Struggles
podcast.body: For a period, Dolores O'Riordan was one of the most famous singers worldwide. However, the immense pressure of the music business, continuous touring, and constant harassment from tabloids and paparazzi led her to suffer a nervous breakdown at the age of 24. She lived a "delicate existence" thereafter, eventually dying in a London hotel room at 46. "And for a while, she was one of the most famous singers in the entire world, male or female. But that didn't work well with her."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dolores O'Riordan's Impact
podcast.body: Dolores O'Riordan, the face and voice of The Cranberries, possessed a powerful and unique vocal style, recognized as one of the most distinctive in the history of alternative rock. She was a significant influence on contemporary artists like Adele, Florence Welch, and Halsey. "Her powerful vocal style was unique and has been called one of the most distinctive voices in the history of Al Rock. Talk to Adele or Florence Welcher, Hallsley, and they'll tell you that Dolores was a huge influence on them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dolores O'Riordan's Six-and-a-Half-Year Separation
podcast.body: Singer Dolores O'Riordan stated she hadn't physically seen "the lads" for six and a half years after the band's initial separation, specifically mentioning Mike Hogan. "I hadn't seen the lads physically for six and a half years, right?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dolores O'Riordan's Vocal Range
podcast.body: Dolores O'Riordan possessed a remarkable vocal talent, characterized by a versatile voice that could transition from "sweet as honey" to "growly and yelpy" as needed. "She had a great voice. It could be a sweet as honey or as growly and yelpy as it needed to be."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dreampop Adjacency
podcast.body: The Cranberries are mentioned as an artist whose music, being dreamy, atmospheric, and immersive, could be "shoehorned" into the Dreampop scene of the late 80s to mid-90s, despite not being core Dreampop.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Discovery and Alternative Roots
podcast.body: The Cranberries were not discovered by a major multinational corporation but emerged from the alternative music scene, signing with Island Records. They worked with The Smiths' producer and had their first John Peel session on the BBC before releasing any album. "los descubrieron Islan Records, habían trabajado con el productor de los Smith, había sido dos también descubiertos por John Pil la primera sesión de los gran bris con John Pil en los vivicis ehs son anteriores a que tuviese ningún disco."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Fan Excitement for Reunion
podcast.body: The band's fans were described as "pumped" and "delighted" about the reunion. "And the fans are called the fans are pumped, they're delighted, you know?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Irish Icon and Activist
podcast.body: Dolores O'Riordan was an icon in Ireland. Before her death in 2018, she was an activist working on behalf of children globally. "She's an icon in Ireland, and before she died in 2018, she worked as an activist on behalf of children all over the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Irish Origin
podcast.body: The band was formed in Limerick, on the West Coast of Ireland, by four teenagers: a couple of brothers, their friend, and Dolores O'Riordan. "They were from Limerick on the West Coast of Ireland. They were formed by four teenagers, a couple of brothers, their friend, and a tiny, feisty woman named Dolores Orreardum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Natural Reunion at Trinity College
podcast.body: Dolores O'Riordan described feeling "really natural" upon seeing her bandmates again at Trinity College, as if she "saw him yesterday," likening the feeling to "a family." "And when I walked in, I just felt really natural. They felt like I saw him yesterday, you know what I mean?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 1

podcast.title: Post-Hype Success and Loyal Fanbase
podcast.body: Following their initial surge in popularity, The Cranberries enjoyed several years of solid success. Five to six years after their major breakthrough, they continued to maintain a faithful fanbase and their distinctive style, refusing to sell out for chart positions. "seguían a 5 o 6 años después del hype siguiendo con una base fiel de seguidores con un estilo propio que no se habían vendido a las listas a cualquier precio."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Reunions and Professionalism
podcast.body: Despite internal disagreements, The Cranberries reunited multiple times, performing songs from Dolores O'Riordan's solo career during these concerts. These reunions were generally well-received by fans, distinguishing them from many other 90s band reunions that were considered mistakes. "cuando se hicieron las reunificaciones de los frambarris llegaron a tocar en los conterdos alguna canción de la trayectoria de solitaría de dolores."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Rise of New Alternative Bands (Mid-90s)
podcast.body: The Cranberries were one of the new bands emerging in the mid-1990s as alternative music gained widespread acceptance. "We had new bands like Weezer and Rage Against the Machine and Beck and the Cranberries in the Verve."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Survival of the Hype
podcast.body: Unlike many bands of their generation that struggled to survive the intense hype of the late 90s (like Republica or No Doubt), The Cranberries built a more solid and slower career path, allowing them to successfully navigate and endure the period of high demand. "fueron una banda que supieron capiar muy bien ese hype del que no sobrevivieron mucha gente."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: The Recurring Couch Motif
podcast.body: A specific rented couch became a distinctive and recurring visual element for The Cranberries' album artwork. It appeared on the covers of their debut album, "Everybody Else Is Doing It, So Why Can't We?" (1993), their second album, "No Need to Argue" (1994), and surprisingly, their 2017 unplugged album, "Something Else." The same couch also made a cameo in the 1996 music video for the Supergrass song "Alright." "The couch disappeared from the Cranberries world until 2017 when it appeared on the cover of the unplugged album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Stories Behind Iconic Album Covers Part 2

podcast.title: Unique Sound in 90s Alt-Rock
podcast.body: Despite not fitting the prevalent guitar-heavy alt-rock sound in North America or the Britpop style in the UK, The Cranberries were signed in 1992 during a period of high demand for alternative bands, and successfully integrated into the growing alt-rock scene. "And even though the cranberries didn't fit with the usual guitar-heavy stuff that was happening in North America, or even the pre-briot pop stuff that was happening in the UK, they nevertheless became part of the growing alt-roxene."

xref.title: Death at London Hilton (January 15, 2018)
xref.body: Dolores O'Riordan died in room 2005 at the London Hilton on Park Lane in Mayfair on January 15, 2018. She had flown from New York to London to work on a solo project titled "Dark" and discuss a new Cranberries album. At 1:12 am, she left an enthusiastic voicemail for a friend about the recording progress, and at 2:00 am, she called her mother, with things appearing fine. She was later found submerged in her bathtub, with numerous empty mini-bar alcohol bottles, an empty champagne bottle, and prescription pills in the room. Toxicology reports indicated that drugs were not an issue, but her blood alcohol content at the time of death was 0.33, more than four times the legal limit for drunk driving. Her death was ruled as accidental drowning due to alcohol toxicity. She was 46. "Dolores or Reardon of the Cranberries... found her submerged in the bathtub."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Last Communications (January 14-15, 2018)
xref.body: On Sunday, January 14, 2018, she emailed The Cranberries guitarist, Noel Hogan, sketches of new songs. At 1:12 AM on January 15, she left a slurred voicemail for her friend Dan Waite, a label executive, expressing great optimism about her life, including a new house and furniture shopping; this voicemail is historically recognized as her final recording. At 3 AM, she spoke to her mother, which was the last time anyone heard from her. "At 1.12am on the morning of the 15th, she left a slurry voicemail for her friend Dan Wait, a labeled executive, saying that she felt very good about everything, including a new house that involved shopping for some furniture."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Andy Rourke Death (May 18, 2023) – Pancreatic Cancer, Age 59; Sued Morrissey, Later Played Two Morrissey Singles
xref.body: Andy Rourke was a founding member of the Smiths and is considered by fans one of the greatest bassists in the history of British indie rock. His time with the band ended badly: a heroin addiction, a lawsuit against Morrissey and Johnny Marr for unpaid royalties (he was broke), and a decade later a bankruptcy over tax issues. Post-Smiths, he worked with the Pretenders, Killing Joke, Stone Roses singer Ian Brown, Dolores O'Riordan and the Cranberries, and Peter Hook of New Order. In a remarkable reconciliation, he played on two Morrissey solo singles despite the money disputes. His father and sister were both diagnosed with cancer, which prompted him to start a cancer charity; he himself was later diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. He died in a New York hospital on May 18, 2023, age 59. "Ask any Smiths fan, and they'll tell you that he was one of the greatest bassists in the history of British Indie Rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Barefoot Performances and Injuries
xref.body: Florence Welch consistently performs barefoot on stage, a preference stemming from her lifelong enjoyment of dancing without shoes. This habit has led to several injuries, including a broken foot sustained from a stage dive during a Coachella gig in April 2015. "Florence, like Dolores Arreared into the cranberries, is one of those people who likes to perform barefoot."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dolores O'Riordan's Approval and Tragic Death
xref.body: Dolores O'Riordan, lead singer of The Cranberries, not only loved Bad Wolves' version of "Zombie" but offered to join them in London to add guitar or background vocals, leaving an excited voice message the night before the planned session. Tragically, she was found dead the next morning, January 15, 2018, having passed out in a bath after heavy drinking. "At the night before, she left a voice message, saying how excited she was about the project, and that she'd see everybody the next day."
